newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo rises again, most Asian markets gain.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo rises again, most Asian markets gain.

text.p: Tokyo's stock market rose for the third consecutive day on Thursday, unperturbed by the prospect of an early general election, and most major Asian bourses gained ground.

Investors in Bangkok ignored political uncertainty over who will be the country's new prime minister and lifted the bourse by 0.76 percent as they sought blue chips, while Hong Kong's key Hang Seng index added 0.28 percent.
But in Bombay, sellers dominated in jittery trade caused by fresh political worries over the fate of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao. The Bombay Stock Exchange lost 1.15 percent.
Brokers said Tokyo stocks finished higher on the back of rising high-technology shares.
The key Nikkei 225 average was up 110.70 points, or 0.52 percent, to end at 21,461.37. Its December futures gained 180 points to 21,550.

"Blue-chips, especially semiconductor shares, remained bullish, and trading volume was heavier today, indicating the market had regained its energy," said Kaoru Ichikawa, a senior trader at Kokusai Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers said that bullish high-tech shares in New York also added to the strong tone in Tokyo.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday he would dissolve parliament's lower house on Friday, paving the way for elections widely expected to be held on October 20.
Ichikawa said market participants would keep an eye on possible deregulation in the telecommunication industry before the election, as this was likely to help buoy stock prices.
Hong Kong stocks ended slightly firmer after a mixed session with selective interest in blue chip issues, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed up 32.60 points at 11,636.13.

"There's moderate volume, but no particular pattern in the market. We have had a damn good run and there is no particular reason to rush in at this point," said Robin Hammond, Hong Kong research director of Asia Equity.
Thai stocks ended up in moderate trade amid a swirl of political rumours as discussions continued over who would be the new prime minister, brokers said.
The SET index ended 7.86 points higher at 1,042.80.
"The index moved in a narrow range as investors carefully bought blue-chip shares despite rumours in the market," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securites.
Political uncertainty has hovered over the market since Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa said on Saturday that he would step down within seven days after choosing a successor.
Brokers said key economic figures, released by the central bank in the afternoon, did not have much impact on the market.
The Bank of Thailand released the current account, trade deficit and other indicators.
Bombay's benchmark index fell 38.42 points to 3,305.50 after a court rejected an anticipatory bail request by Rao against possible arrest in a criminal conspiracy case.
Taiwan share prices closed 1.08 percent higher in light trade as the overnight rebound by U.S. high-technology issues triggered active buying in blue chip electronics, brokers said.
But caution ahead of a three-day weekend kept the index from rising further, brokers said. The market is closed on Friday and Saturday for the Mid-Autumn Festival.
The weighted index advanced 1.08 percent, or 69.65 points, to 6,508.17.
The Australian share market's All Ordinaries index added 20.6 points, or 0.91 percent, to 2273.4, but Jakarta's Composite Index fell 1.03 points, or 0.18 percent, to 571.26 points.
Seoul's market was closed and will reopen on Monday.
At 1140 GMT, the dollar was at 110.50/0.60 yen and 1.5214/19 marks.
Bullion ended at US$382.00/50, against New York's US$382.40/80 close on Wednesday.
SIMEX North Sea Brent crude oil futures for November were steady and last traded at $23.20 a barrel.
